case: The business identity triple carries no uniqueness constraint, so two concurrent allocations both validate and both release.
why: This is the measured state: `identity.key` was the surrogate `(company_id, record_id, revision)`, the triple 05 section 6 declares as the identity was three ordinary payload fields, and `natural_key`, `unique` and `uniqueness` occurred nowhere in record-registry.json. The registry HAS the construct and uses it on the immediate neighbours -- nine of 188 records declare an exclusive factory, and `SendClaim`'s invariant reads "one-use claim ... it cannot authorize a second dispatch" -- and none of the fifteen new records declared anything. For fourteen that is harmless; for the one record whose entire purpose is convergence under concurrency it is the mechanism.
expect_failure_contains: DOES NOT CONSTRAIN ITS BUSINESS TRIPLE
